layer1.name: ChairFill
layer1.one_liner: Cancellation backfill for independent hair salons.
layer1.description: Fills cancelled appointment slots from a standby list. Every assumption in the ledger reached its pre-registered sample size, so the cap sits at its ceiling and stops mattering.
layer1.outcome_note: Synthetic fixture. Not a real company and not counted toward separation statistics.

layer2.pins: The top of the cap's range, end to end. Every assumption reaches its sample size, so Evidence Quality is 100 and the cap is exactly 100 — the formula's ceiling, which constants.test.ts asserts arithmetically but nothing else demonstrates through the runner. capBinding must be false: at full coverage the cap stops constraining anything and the composite is set entirely by the evidence. This is what a founder who did the work is supposed to see, and it is the counterpart to synth-001, where the same pipeline is held to 30.

assumptions.statement: At least 5 in 10 independent hair salons with 3 or more chairs lose more than 4 appointment slots a week to cancellations

falsification_criterion.applies_to: independent hair salons with 3 or more chairs
falsification_criterion.observation: ask the owner to pull last month's cancellation count from their booking system
falsification_criterion.metric: count losing more than 4 slots a week

assumptions.statement: At least 3 in 10 independent salon owners already pay above $50 a month for booking software

falsification_criterion.observation: ask them to list their current software line items and cost

assumptions.statement: At least 3 in 10 independent salons contacted through beauty supply distributor lists reply within a week

falsification_criterion.applies_to: independent salons on beauty supply distributor lists
falsification_criterion.observation: contact listed salons and count replies within a week

assumptions.statement: No incumbent salon booking system ships automated standby backfill within 12 months

falsification_criterion.applies_to: the three most-used salon booking systems
falsification_criterion.observation: review release notes and pricing pages for standby backfill

assumptions.statement: The founder can complete at least 2 salon onboardings a week without an on-site visit

falsification_criterion.observation: log how many completed onboarding remotely each week

claims.text: A salon owner pulled 6 cancelled slots for the previous week from their booking system.
A second owner reports about 5 cancellations a week and keeps an informal standby list on paper.
A third owner describes cancellations as their largest controllable revenue loss.
A fourth owner reports fewer than 2 a week after introducing deposits.
An owner lists booking software and a payments tool, both above the threshold.
A second owner confirms monthly booking software spend well above $50.
A third owner names three paid tools in their monthly stack.
A distributor-listed salon replied within two days and booked a call.
A second listed salon replied the same week without a warm introduction.
A third listed salon replied after a follow-up.
A booking vendor's product lead confirmed standby backfill is not on their roadmap.
A second vendor's partner manager described backfill as out of scope for them.
A third vendor's reseller confirmed no backfill capability in the current release.
The largest vendor's pricing page lists no standby or waitlist feature at any tier.
claims.retrieved_text: Synthetic fixture text. Not retrieved from any real source.

claims.text: Two salons completed onboarding over a video call in the first week.
A third salon completed onboarding remotely the following week.
